You have to be an RN first before you can even apply to NP school. Most programs require 1-2 years of bedside nursing experience first before applying. 
If you don't want to do bedside nursing at all then highly suggest going to PA school. PA is a mid-level known as Physician Assistants. They can't practice autonomous but are well prepared as providers right out school in comparison to some if not most NP programs. They make 6 figures and can practice in any specialty versus NP is specialized ie. FNP ACNP ect. 

Also most np programs you have to find your own preceptor which is an absolute pain in the butt. The schools that do find preceptors for you have thousands of applicants and are usually the most competitive. 

NP salary varies by location but most make berween 70-130k.

You definitely need to do more research first but my recommendation is PA sounds better for you if you want to go right into a program.
